404 with no body is 'nothing under that key', not a failure.

A segment is never a filter (rule 5): widgets/all is GET widgets?participant=all. It answers the WidgetsFrame every widgets read answers (fm-server WidgetV1Controller), not widgets/all's bare list: 0.4.0 to 0.11.0 read a list here and failed on every call.
The catalogue a launch form is built from, and what fm-capm reads to see how the MVO robots' penalty is set. A collection under its marketplace, read with GET.
A fixed parameter is a PUT of the value alone: the server reads any bound as a control, so an SDK that sent min/max/step as null would be asking for something else.
An exposed parameter sends its control flat beside the value, as the server's ParameterRequest reads it; nested under 'control' the server would see no bounds and fix it.

A call market is the same POST as any market, with the mechanism and its schedule in the body; left out, the server makes a continuous market and nothing says so.
Clear now creates a call where the calls are listed (fm-server 4.17, R5): POST the marketplace's calls with the market in the body. The market's own calls route is superseded.
The history is the marketplace's, across its call markets: GET calls under the marketplace, not under a market.
One session's calls are a filter, so a query parameter (rule 5), spelled ?sessions= as on every other list since fm-server 4.17 (Q1); ?sessionId= is still read for older SDKs.

A page is ?limit= on the collection's own route (fm-server 4.17, P1), and the next page's before is the one the Link header names: without reading it a caller cannot tell a full last page from one with older rows behind it.
The first page of a marketplace's sessions: the newest two, oldest first as the whole list is, and Link: rel="next" while older ones remain.
A full page with no Link is the last. A client that guessed the next before from the oldest row would read one more, empty page -- or loop, against a server whose rows are not dense.
orders() reads the lifecycle less cancellations (?cancelled=false); its page must keep that filter, or a page of orders holds rows the whole read never did.
before is sent as given, and the next page's comes from the Link, not from the request.
A short page is the last: no Link, so next is null.
The admin's account list pages like every other growing collection.
A marketplace's calls grow with every clear; their page is under the marketplace, as calls() is.
